unrelated species as pets. We don't have anybody's poodle.
Anyway, if you've overturned your bookcase this month (as H tends to do, I must admit), take a break and flip through Very Interesting. I think you’ll love it.
On a lighter note, H is still learning to handle being chased by a dog. He has formed bonds with many canines in two of our local dog parks and is named as the dog's favorite person without exception.
At times I feel jealous or skeptical, but as these particular dogs are small, and the majority consists of Westies, I invariably get intimidated initially. But then I remind myself that I am three times their size, so there's no reason to be jealous... yet if I had a Pekingese, that would be a different story.
I find my furry children endlessly captivating, especially how shocked those around them are – unending energy and universally positive moods, compared to ours, hehe… Even Britt just amplifies their fascination every day.
Doesn't Britt with her Westie make a pretty pair, thou...? I shall write an entire manuscript, it seems that H is the talk of the town, I suppose? Though with a choice of boot size being 5 cent or perhaps not, and without knowing for sure, I commented, did I resemble a Canadian redneck? It seems I exceeded the limit, perhaps regarding care of pets, and it came back to me similarly.
I believe big dog followers leave more tracks than cats at first, though I might be mistaken, but the two unrelated strangers at the dog segment (a German and a British one?) I believe Britt cannot resist this fur ball… but what about H?! She properly mounts his dam legs in a manner similar to a dog — lol.
While genetics influences animal adoption, the sandpaper-like texture of the tongue is highly favored — that’s where our differences lie compared to dogs, and my texture isn’t as rough.
I have my sandpaper tongue ready for extra care when needed!
